jurisdiction.name: Syrian Arab Republic
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Syria has no AI-specific law, strategy, ethics framework or regulator guidance with an official text online as of October 2026. The one binding instrument that governs AI inputs is the Personal Data Protection Law (Law No. 12 of 2024, in force since 1 January 2025), which sets consent-based processing rules, data-subject rights and a Personal Data Protection Authority attached to the communications ministry. Digital policy is led by the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MoCT), with the National Agency for Information Technology Services (NAITS) publishing ICT laws, information-security policy and technical regulations, none of which mention AI. A national AI strategy discussed under the previous government (2022–2024) was never published as an official document, and since the 2025 transitional government MoCT has promoted AI through conferences and partnerships rather than published policy. Recorded leads include the 2024 executive instructions of the data protection law and the 2021 digital transformation strategy for government services.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MoCT)
National Agency for Information Technology Services (NAITS)
narrative.review_notes: Deep review completed on 7 October 2026, using the official ICT-law texts published by the national information-technology agency; the electronic-transactions and cybercrime laws and the information-security policy contain no AI provisions. Material of the communications ministry, central bank, Prime Minister's office, higher-education ministry, People's Assembly and telecom regulator remains to be checked, and a pre-2024 national AI strategy is listed as a lead because no official text or issuing body has been found.

instruments.current_status: Issued in Damascus on 28 March 2024 (People's Assembly session of 18 March 2024); Article 46 makes it effective from 1 January 2025. Executive Instructions were issued by Prime Ministerial decision in 2024 (see leads). Enacted under the pre-December-2024 government; no repeal or amendment found by 2026-10-07, but its application under the transitional authorities and the status of the Personal Data Protection Authority were not confirmed from an official source.
instruments.scope: Electronic processing of personal data by public and private controllers and processors in Syria
instruments.summary: Syria's general personal data law, covering electronic collection and processing of personal data. It bans processing or disclosure without the data subject's explicit consent except where the law permits, grants rights of access, correction, erasure, objection to processing or its results, and complaint, and requires controllers and processors to hold a licence or permit, appoint a data protection officer and apply approved security standards. It creates the Personal Data Protection Authority, attached to the Minister of Communications and Technology, which regulates processing and cross-border transfers; the law contains no AI-specific provisions but governs personal data used to train and run AI systems.

instruments.official_title: القرار التنظيمي 24/ت الخاص بترخيص التطبيقات الصحية الإلكترونية
instruments.english_title: Ministry of Health Regulatory Decision No. 24/T of 2025 on the licensing of electronic health applications
instruments.issuing_authority: Minister of Health (Ministry of Health of the Syrian Arab Republic)
instruments.current_status: Signed by Minister of Health Dr. Musab Nazzal al-Ali in Damascus in 2025; the day and month of signature are handwritten on the scanned original (they appear to read 2/12/2025) and are not used. Article 7 repeals Regulatory Decision No. 13/T of 2023 and orders publication in the Official Gazette (gazette reference not found). A Ministry of Health circular of September 2026 (No. 19/2449) requires owners of existing health apps to apply for a licence by 2 December 2026, after which unlicensed apps face suspension.
instruments.scope: Mobile and web applications that provide medical or health services to users in Syria, their owners, scientific supervisors and data protection officers
instruments.summary: Ministerial regulatory decision setting the licensing regime for electronic health applications: apps need Ministry of Health approval and accreditation by the National Agency for Information Technology Services, must name a scientific supervisor and a data protection officer, host patient data on servers inside Syria, and may be suspended for breaches. Among the general conditions (Article 3), apps must not use artificial intelligence as a source of clinical information without review by the app's medical team, which makes human clinical oversight of AI output a licensing requirement.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding health-sector rule with an explicit AI provision: AI may not be used as a source of clinical information in licensed health apps without verification by the medical team.
metadata_gaps: Exact signature date (handwritten on the scan; only the printed year 2025 used)

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Official sites (the national information-technology agency, the justice, health, education and other ministries and the standards body) were searched in Arabic and English, and no official AI-specific text was found in any category except data protection law and one health ministry decision. A reported pre-2024 national AI strategy and a media code of conduct with an AI article are listed as leads. The UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI applies through the regional file.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Method note (original): Deep review completed on 7 October 2026. The national information-technology agency publishes the official texts of the ICT laws, and these were read. The websites of the communications ministry, the central bank, the Prime Minister's office, the higher-education ministry, the People's Assembly and the telecom regulator could not be read. The electronic-transactions and cybercrime laws and the information-security policy contain no AI provisions. A pre-2024 national AI strategy is pending because no official text or issuing body has been found.

Coverage note (original): Searched official sites (NAITS, Ministry of Justice, SASMO, Ministry of Health, Ministry of Education portal) and search engines in Arabic and English; MoCT, Central Bank, Prime Ministry and parliament sites could not be read automatically. No official AI-specific text found in any category except data protection law. The UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI applies via the regional file. Technical review notes: Deep review 2026-10-07. moct.gov.sy, cb.gov.sy, pministry.gov.sy and mohe.gov.sy failed automated reading (TLS chain not verifiable / HTTP 503 to the fetcher); parliament.gov.sy, nans.gov.sy, mic.gov.sy and gov.sy were unreachable; sytra.gov.sy serves only a hosting placeholder page. NAITS (naits.gov.sy/laws) was readable and hosts the official texts of the ICT laws. Not recorded as AI instruments after reading the official texts (no AI provisions): Electronic Transactions Law No. 3 of 2014 (defines an automated 'electronic agent' but nothing AI-specific), Cybercrime Law No. 20 of 2022 (Ministry of Justice Circular No. 26 of 2026 now governs its procedures), Law No. 7 of 2023 establishing NAITS, the National Information Security Policy, and NAITS accreditation rules for electronic applications and information systems. SASMO's standards catalogue has no AI standard (no ISO/IEC 42001 adoption). Ministry of Health strategic plan and Ministry of Education pages have no AI policy text. The pre-2024 'National AI Strategy' is known only from state-newspaper reports (Al-Thawra, December 2024) with no issuing body or official text; held as a lead. News agencies and newspapers (SANA, Al-Watan, Al-Thawra) were used only for discovery. The UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI applies through the UNESCO regional file. Ministry catch-up 2026-10-13 (PROTOCOL §2 ministry rule, applied after this country's deep review; one agent, 30 minutes, national ministries' own AI documents only, nothing else re-reviewed): 1 record(s) added. Ministries: Ministry of Health (moh.gov.sy): Regulatory Decision 24/T of 2025 on licensing electronic health apps, with an AI clinical-information rule (recorded); strategic plan, digital transformation and health-app pages checked, no other AI document. Ministry of Education: site unreachable (moe.gov.sy, curl and WebFetch 503); searches found nothing. Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research: site unreachable (mohe.gov.sy, curl and WebFetch 503); searches found only university research papers, no ministry AI rules. Ministry of Justice (moj.gov.sy): site search and circulars/decisions pages checked; nothing found. Ministry of Defence: site unreachable; searches found nothing. Ministry of Finance / tax / customs: site unreachable (mof.gov.sy); searches found nothing. Ministry of Interior: site is a holding page; nothing found. Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates (mofaex.gov.sy): homepage checked, nothing new (2023 Global AI Governance Initiative statement already a lead). Ministry of Social Affairs and Labour: site unreachable; nothing found. Ministry of Administrative Development: site unreachable; searches found employee database and training-policy work, no AI guidance. Ministry of Communications and Technology: site unreachable (moct.gov.sy, curl and WebFetch 503); searches found conferences and MoUs only, no AI document; NAITS laws page PDFs re-checked, none mention AI. Ministry of Information: Professional and Ethical Code of Conduct for the Media Sector (Feb 2026) reportedly has an AI article; no official text found (new lead). Ministries of Agriculture, Transport, Culture (homepages reachable) and Economy, Energy, Tourism, Water Resources (unreachable): nothing found.. Not reached: Ministry of Education (moe.gov.sy unreachable); Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research (mohe.gov.sy unreachable); Ministry of Communications and Technology (moct.gov.sy unreachable); Ministry of Finance (mof.gov.sy unreachable); Ministry of Administrative Development, Social Affairs and Labour, Defence, Economy, Tourism, Water Resources (sites unreachable; web search only); Ministry of Information (website not identified). Could not verify: Ministry of Information media code of conduct text (AI article) - no official copy found; Ministry of Education, Higher Education, Communications, Finance sites unreachable (curl and WebFetch).
